source: Hi Dana, no rush but if you get a chance could you maybe take a look at the Q3 numbers before Thursday's meeting? Thanks!

meaning.implied: "No rush" is politeness; the numbers are needed before the meeting.

rewrite: Hi Dana, could you please review the Q3 numbers before Thursday's meeting? Thanks!
notes: Made the request direct: please review the Q3 numbers.
"No rush" hid a real deadline, so it now reads clearly: before Thursday's meeting.

source: Why is the vendor report still not done? I needed it yesterday.

meaning.ask: Send the vendor report, or explain the delay
meaning.implied: The sender is frustrated that the report is late.

rewrite: I needed the vendor report yesterday and still don't have it. Could you send it right away, or tell me what's holding it up? I'm frustrated it's late.
notes: Turned the question into a clear ask: send it or explain the delay.
Said the frustration out loud so it isn't left to guesswork.

source: I hope you're doing well! I was just wondering whether it might be possible, if it's not too much trouble, to perhaps get the signed contract back from you at some point this week?

meaning.implied: This is a request with a deadline, not an optional favour.

rewrite: I hope you're doing well! Could you please send the signed contract back to me this week?
notes: Removed the layers of hedging so the request is easy to spot.
Kept the deadline exactly as given: this week.

source: The team meeting has moved to Friday at 10:00 in Room 4. Please bring your project updates.

meaning.ask: Bring your project updates to the meeting

rewrite: The team meeting has moved to Friday at 10:00 in Room 4. Please bring your project updates.

source:
Q: Are you coming to the team lunch on Friday?
Reply: I've got a dentist appointment that afternoon.

meaning.implied: The answer is no: the sender can't come to the lunch.

rewrite: No, I can't come to the team lunch on Friday. I've got a dentist appointment that afternoon.
notes: Stated the answer directly: you can't come.
Kept the reason so it still reads as a friendly decline.
